summary: 7 Wonders is a fast-paced card drafting game where you build a civilization by picking one card from a hand and passing the rest, repeating until your city takes shape across three ages. It runs almost entirely in parallel with your neighbors, punctuated by quick resource-cost checks and occasional military comparisons, culminating in a broad points tally across military, science, commerce, guilds, and wonders.
praised: Extremely fast turns with no downtime despite the player count
Scales smoothly from 3 to 7 players with consistent playtime
High variety from different wonders, card combos, and set collection paths
Low rules overhead for the strategic depth it offers
criticised: Limited direct interaction beyond your two neighbors, which can feel solitaire-like
Military and science can snowball or feel swingy if under-drafted early
Symbol-heavy iconography has a steep initial learning curve
Card text/effects require some memorization or reference early on

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with limited neighbor-only conflict

scoring.why: final score sums civilian buildings, coins, wonders, military conflict tokens, science sets, and guild bonuses, so no single track dominates
